doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

title: James Taylor: the 2001 'Mean Old Man' date and Bucky's reaction
summary: Russ Titelman called him for a session in August 2001. He played rhythm guitar behind James Taylor, with Jimmy Johnson, Larry Goldings and Steve Gadd, and Bucky asked who the rhythm player was.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: You also mentioned — it’s time to mention working with James Taylor and you spoke about his distinctive guitar playing which I found to be very interesting.

Well we did — the first part was Russ Titelman called me to play, do a date for him in August of 2001. And it was down at Clinton. And he had a song called “Mean Old Man.” And I was in the booth with my guitar and James came into the thing and he was showing me the chords. They had sort of a nutty chord sheet and James came in and he went — and he always whistles like, playing all the chords. And I’m going this is James Taylor sitting in front of me. And I could see Russ Titelman on the other side, outside the booth looking at me like, “Don’t start crying or anything, just pay attention. Can you please do that much?” And so we did the thing and I remember I actually played the verse with him on that.
